thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: sev2 — multiple GPU host reboots observed in us-central1-a (host pool: hosted-inference-prod). Elevated 5xx and tail latency. Pagerduty incident created PD-4821. Please acknowledge and triage. :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): Acked. I’m on it. Linking grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/hosts/reboots?var-zone=us-central1-a — seeing spike at ~2035647600 UTC.

lee (sre): I’m pulling host logs and dmesg. Initial glance shows repeated PCIe AER corrected errors for a single host then kernel triggered GPU driver reset. snippet:```kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.4: AER: Corrected error received: ID 00e0
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
kernel: nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU recovery succeeded
```

jordan (eng-runtime): That looks like a noisy neighbor causing ECC/PCIe errors and then the driver reset. If the runtime sees a GPU disappear drivers often return 13/500 from the model server. Can we failover traffic to fallback model variant and drain the node? Suggest route change: shift hosted-inference-prod -> fallback pool for latency-sensitive routes.

maya (oncall): Will run the route shift. Doing canary: 10% -> fallback. Using console quick actions.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: routing-change hosted-inference-prod canary=10 -> fallback-pool (job id: deploy-8745).

maya (oncall): Canary looks good at 10% for 2m. Latency stable, errors drop for those users. Increasing to 50%.

nora (support): Which customers are in the impacted cohort? I have two high-touch customers showing increased 5xx: acme-inc and luma-ai. Informing CSMs and opening support tickets.

lee (sre): Collecting host-level traces. Full dmesg + nvidia-smi -q output attached (pasted):```============NVSMI LOG===========Timestamp                           : Sun Mar 15 20:06:34 2026
Timestamp                                   : 2026-03-15T20:06:34Z
GPU 00000000:65:00.0
    Product Name                            : NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
    ECC Errors
        Volatile                                                                                  : 124
        Aggregate                                                                                 : 124
    Reset Count                              : 3
```

alex (infra): I queried cloud provider events for us-central1-a — there's a recent maintenance window for accelerated compute started 2035647000-2035647400 (provider maintenance id: GCP-MAINT-9982). Filing to provider support, but those windows sometimes correlate with underlying firmware updates.

jordan (eng-runtime): Given ECC counts + resets we should: 1) cordon + drain affected host from autoscaler pools, 2) reprovision replacements, 3) pin customers to Dedicated if they need isolation (note for sales). For immediate mitigation I recommend full shift to fallback pool until we reprovision the bad host(s).

maya (oncall): cordon/drain executed for host host-uc-a-112:```kubectl cordon host-uc-a-112 && kubectl drain host-uc-a-112 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l pool=hosted-inference-prod``` Drain completed, pods rescheduled. Observed some restart flaps on a model server that hit transient OOM; increased restart backoff.

lee (sre): Captured stack traces from the kernel around reset:```Mar 15 20:05:22 host-uc-a-112 kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.4: AER: Multiple Corrected error, status=0x00004000
Mar 15 20:05:22 host-uc-a-112 kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00: nvlink: timeout waiting for link training
Mar 15 20:05:23 host-uc-a-112 kernel: nvidia: reset: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has reset (reason: link timeout)
Mar 15 20:06:05 host-uc-a-112 kernel: kernel: pci_bus 0000:65: scanning bus - parent bus crashed previously
```

jordan (eng-runtime): Hypotheses: A) Cloud maintenance pushed microcode/firmware causing transient PCIe errors -> driver reset. B) Hardware noisy neighbor causing thermal/voltage instability -> ECC buildup -> reset. C) Driver regression (less likely given provider maintenance ID). We need to repro by reprovisioning host or migrating customers off that HW type.

alex (infra): I'm requesting immediate host replacement from provider and asking for HW telemetry, also opening an infra ticket to repro allocate new host with same SKU and run burn-in. Ticket: INFRA-1129.

nora (support): Customer comms: Sending a short note to acme-inc and luma-ai: "We noticed elevated 5xx and tail latency; we've shifted your traffic to fallback and are investigating host-level GPU resets. We will follow up with RCA."

maya (oncall): Quick customer impact summary for incident timeline: 20:04-20:12 UTC — elevated 5xx for hosted API, ~2.3% of requests globally, affected two enterprise tenants. Mitigation (20:06) route shift & drain reduced errors to <0.1% by 20:10.

lee (sre): Attaching full log snippets to PD-4821 and to the incident doc. Adding timeline entries:```2035647000 provider maint start (possible correlate)
2035647560 first GPU reset detected on host-uc-a-112
2035647622 escalation + pagerduty
2035647660 cordon/drain host-uc-a-112
2035647720 canary routing shift 10%
2035647785 routing shift 50%
2035647800 errors fall to baseline for majority
```

jordan (eng-runtime): Action items: - jordan: validate model-server handles GPU detach gracefully (task ENG-2250) - lee: collect and upload full kernel+nvidia logs, coordinate with provider (SRE-331) - alex: request host replacement and burn-in (INFRA-1129) - nora: customer follow-up and SOC ticket link (SUP-887)

maya (oncall): Handing off to follow-up RCA channel: #postmortems. Next steps: full RCA within 72h, include provider response and host telemetry. Closing active pager for now — keep thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
